name: Beating
overview: The Scriptures present beating both as a form of human punishment and as a consequence of faithful witness for Christ. In the Old Testament, beatings served as a disciplinary measure, limited by law to prevent excessive harm, as seen in Deuteronomy 25:3. The New Testament records believers like the apostles receiving beatings for their testimony and obedience to Jesus, exemplified in Acts 5:40 and Acts 16:22, highlighting the cost of discipleship. These passages collectively show that while beating was used as punishment, believers are called to endure it for the sake of the gospel.
